{{Short description|Finnish evolutionary ecologist}}
'''Riitta Johanna Mappes'''  (born 13 October 1965 in Valkeakoski, Finland) is an [[Evolutionary ecology|evolutionary ecologist]] based in [[Finland]]. Her research focuses on interspecific interactions, such as those between [[Predation|predators and prey]]. She is known for her work on the evolution of [[Aposematism|aposematic signals]] and [[mimicry]] in chemically defended prey, the evolution of [[Signalling theory|signal]] [[Polymorphism (biology)|polymorphism]], the evolution of bacterial [[virulence]], and the evolution of [[Sexual reproduction|sexual]] and [[Asexual reproduction|asexual]] reproduction.<ref name="J-Mappes-publications">{{Cite web|last=Mappes|first=Johanna|date=|title=Google Scholar citations for Johanna Mappes|url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?hl=en&user=Fus_SqEAAAAJ&view_op=list_works&sortby=pubdate|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2020-11-25|website=scholar.google.com}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web|last=Mappes|first=Johanna|date=|title=Research Gate profile of Johanna Mappes|url=https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Johanna_Mappes|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2020-11-25|website=Research Gate}}</ref> Her main study species include the wood tiger moth (''[[Parasemia plantaginis|Arctia plantaginis]]''), vipers ([[Viperidae]]), the [[Colorado potato beetle]] (''Leptinotarsa decemlineata'') and the drumming wolf-spider (''Hygrolycosa rubrofasciata'').<ref name="J-Mappes-publications" /><ref name=":0" />

Mappes earned her MSc degree in 1991 and her PhD in 1994, both from the [[University of Jyväskylä]], Finland. Her doctoral thesis focused on reproductive tactics and maternal care in [[shield bug]]s, particularly the [[parent bug]] (''Elasmucha grisea''). In 2003 The [[Academy of Finland]] awarded Mappes the '''Young Dynamic Researcher Award''<nowiki/>' for her research merits in developing the ‘[[novel world method]]’ to study the evolution of [[aposematism]].<ref>{{cite press release|last=Tirronen|first=Riitta|title=Akatemian kannustuspalkinto Johanna Mappesille - Uusi tutkimusmenetelmä toi uutta tietoa eliöiden varoitusväreistä|language=Finnish|date=18 November 2003|publisher=Academy of Finland|url=http://www.aka.fi/fi/A/Suomen-Akatemia/Mediapalvelut/Tiedotteet/Tiedotteet-2003/Uusi-tutkimusmenetelma-toi-uutta-tietoa-elioiden-varoitusvareista/|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130217113344/http://www.aka.fi/fi/A/Suomen-Akatemia/Mediapalvelut/Tiedotteet/Tiedotteet-2003/Uusi-tutkimusmenetelma-toi-uutta-tietoa-elioiden-varoitusvareista/|url-status=dead|archive-date=17 February 2013|accessdate=2013-01-22}}</ref>

She was elected as a Research Professor at the [[Academy of Finland]] from 2009-2013, and again from 2019-2023.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=Academy of Finland selects 10 new - Academy of Finland|url=https://www.aka.fi/en/about-us/whats-new/press-releases/2018/academy-of-finland-selects-10-new-academy-professors/?_t_id=fHqYm4TCJtN7WbZejBN7dQ==&_t_uuid=w40YzP5JSUSYRKMtbQdcAA&_t_q=Johanna+Mappes&_t_tags=language:en,siteid:89e2ba17-5f81-4e18-a6e2-27ce1774d3e5,andquerymatch&_t_hit.id=AkaFi_Web_Models_Pages_NewsPage/_a300cc6b-4f09-4568-9c65-e2340d871a27_en&_t_hit.pos=11|access-date=2020-11-26|website=www.aka.fi}}</ref> Mappes served as a Professor of Evolutionary Ecology at the [[University of Jyväskylä]] from 2008-2019, where she headed the ''Centre of Excellence in Biological Interactions'' for the [[Academy of Finland]] from 2012-2018.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Centre of Excellence in Biological Interactions|url=https://www.jyu.fi/science/en/bioenv/research/coe-interactions/centre-of-excellence-in-biologican-interactions|access-date=2020-11-25|website=Matemaattis-luonnontieteellinen tiedekunta|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Centres of Excellence in Research 2012‒2017|url=http://www.aka.fi/en-GB/A/Programmes-and-cooperation/Centres-of-Excellence-/Ongoing/Finnish-Programme-for-Centres-of-Excellence-in-Research-20122017-second-round-of-application/|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130217112400/http://www.aka.fi/en-GB/A/Programmes-and-cooperation/Centres-of-Excellence-/Ongoing/Finnish-Programme-for-Centres-of-Excellence-in-Research-20122017-second-round-of-application/|archive-date=17 February 2013|accessdate=22 January 2013|publisher=Academy of Finland}}</ref> In 2017 she was elected member of the [[Finnish Society of Sciences and Letters]]<ref>{{Cite web|title=Finnish Society of Sciences and Letters: List of Members|url=https://scientiarum.fi/wp-content/uploads/2021/08/Ordinarie-ledamoter-27.8.2021.pdf}}</ref> and in 2018 she became an honorary member of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] (AAAS).<ref>{{Cite web|title=Johanna Mappes|url=https://www.amacad.org/person/johanna-mappes|access-date=2020-11-25|website=American Academy of Arts & Sciences|language=en}}</ref> In 2019 she was invited to membership in the Royal Physiographic Society of Lund. As of 2020, she is a Professor of Ecology at the [[University of Helsinki]], Research Professor at the [[Academy of Finland]],<ref name=":1" /> and member of the governing board for the [[Finnish Academy of Science and Letters]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Board of the Academy|url=https://www.acadsci.fi/en/about-the-academy/organization/board-of-the-academy.html|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2020-11-25|website=Finnish Academy of Science and Letters|language=en-gb}}</ref>
